sentences.zh: 杜彥杜彥，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Du Yan—Du Yan was a native of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan was from Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 父遷，屬葛榮之亂，徙家於幽。

translations.literal: His father Qian, during Ge Rong's rebellion, moved the family to You.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian had moved the family to You during the turmoil of Ge Rong's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 彥性勇果，善騎射。

translations.literal: Yan by nature was brave and resolute, skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was by nature courageous and decisive, and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 仕周，釋褐左侍上士，後從柱國陸通擊陳將吳明徹於土州，破之。

translations.literal: He served Zhou; upon first appointment he became Left Attendant Upper Gentleman; later he followed the pillar of state Lu Tong to attack the Chen general Wu Mingche at Tuzhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Zhou service and received his first appointment as Left Attendant Upper Gentleman; later he followed the pillar of state Lu Tong in an attack on the Chen general Wu Mingche at Tuzhou and routed him.

sentences.zh: 又擊叛蠻，克倉塠、白楊二柵，並斬其渠帥。

translations.literal: Again he attacked rebellious tribes, captured the two stockades Cangchi and Baiyang, and beheaded their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against rebellious tribes, taking the stockades at Cangchi and Baiyang and beheading their leaders.

sentences.zh: 進平郢州賊帥樊志，以戰功拜大都督。

translations.literal: Advancing, he pacified the Yingzhou bandit leader Fan Zhi; for battle merit he was appointed grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: In a further advance he subdued the bandit chief Fan Zhi in Yingzhou and, for his military achievements, was made a grand commander.

sentences.zh: 尋遷儀同，治隆山郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to yitong rank and administered Longshan commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to yitong and put in charge of Longshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜隴州刺史，賜爵永安縣伯。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed inspector of Longzhou and granted the title Baron of Yong'an county.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed inspector of Longzhou and ennobled as Baron of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉迥於相州，每戰有功，賜物三千段，奴婢三十口。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan to attack Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou; in every battle he had merit, and was granted three thousand bolts of goods and thirty household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was still grand chancellor, Yan followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou; he distinguished himself in every engagement and was rewarded with three thousand bolts of silk and thirty household slaves.

sentences.zh: 進位上開府，改封襄武縣侯，拜魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He advanced in rank to upper director of departments, was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangwu county, and appointed administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to upper director of departments, created Marquis of Xiangwu, and appointed administrator of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，授丹州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed inspector of Danzhou and advanced in enfeoffment to duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era he was made inspector of Danzhou and advanced to ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 後六歲，征為左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Six years later he was summoned to be general of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was recalled to serve as general of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管與新義公韓擒相繼而進。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, as campaign commander he advanced in succession with the Duke of Xinyi, Han Qin.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he served as campaign commander, advancing in turn with Han Qin, Duke of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 軍至南陵，賊屯據江岸，彥遣儀同樊子蓋率精兵擊破其柵，獲船六百餘艘。

translations.literal: The army reached Nanling; rebels were stationed on the riverbank; Yan sent the yitong Fan Zigai leading elite troops to smash their palisade and captured more than six hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Nanling, enemy forces held the riverbank. Yan sent Fan Zigai, a yitong officer, with picked troops to break their stockade and seized more than six hundred vessels.

sentences.zh: 渡江，擊南陵城，拔之，擒其守將許翼。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he attacked Nanling city, took it, and captured its defending general Xu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi, stormed Nanling, took the city, and captured its commandant, Xu Yi.

sentences.zh: 進至新林，與擒合軍。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xinlin, he joined armies with Han Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Xinlin and united his forces with Han Qin's.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，賜物五千段，粟六千石，進位柱國，賜子寶安爵昌陽縣公。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was granted five thousand bolts of goods and six thousand shi of grain, advanced to pillar of state, and his son Bao'an was granted the title Duke of Changyang county.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was subdued he received five thousand bolts of goods and six thousand shi of grain, was promoted to pillar of state, and his son Bao'an was ennobled as Duke of Changyang.

sentences.zh: 高智慧等之作亂也，複以行軍總管從楊素討之，別解江州圍。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rose in rebellion, again as campaign commander he followed Yang Su to suppress them and separately relieved the siege of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled, he again served as campaign commander under Yang Su and on his own broke the siege of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 智慧餘黨往往屯聚，保投溪洞，彥水陸兼進，攻錦山、陽父、若、石壁四洞，悉平之，皆斬其渠帥。

translations.literal: Zhihui's remnant partisans often gathered and took refuge in stream caves; Yan advanced by land and water together, attacked the four caves Jinshan, Yangfu, Ruo, and Shibi, pacified them all, and beheaded their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui's scattered followers often gathered in mountain ravines and cave strongholds. Yan advanced by land and river alike, stormed the four strongholds of Jinshan, Yangfu, Ruo, and Shibi, reduced them all, and executed their leaders.

sentences.zh: 賊李陀擁眾數千，據彭山，彥襲擊破之，斬陀，傳其首。

translations.literal: The bandit Li Tuo mustered several thousand followers and held Pengshan; Yan made a surprise attack and defeated him, beheaded Tuo, and forwarded his head.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Li Tuo rallied several thousand men and held Pengshan. Yan surprised and routed him, killed Tuo, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又擊徐州、宜豐二洞，悉平之。

translations.literal: Again he attacked the two caves Xuzhou and Yifeng and pacified them completely.
translations.idiomatic: He also subdued the strongholds at Xuzhou and Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢百餘口。

translations.literal: He was granted more than a hundred household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with more than a hundred slaves.

sentences.zh: 拜洪州總管，甚有治名。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor-general of Hongzhou and had a great reputation for governance.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed governor-general of Hongzhou, he won a strong reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，雲州總管賀婁子幹卒，上悼惜者久之，因謂侍臣曰：「榆林國之重鎮，安得子幹之輩乎？

translations.literal: After more than a year, Yunzhou governor-general Helou Zigan died; the emperor mourned him long, and thus said to attending ministers: "Yulin is a vital post for the state—where can one find men of Zigan's caliber?"
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later the governor-general of Yunzhou, Helou Zigan, died. The emperor mourned him at length and said to his attendants, "Yulin is a strategic linchpin of the realm—where shall we find another man like Zigan?"

sentences.zh: 」後數日，上曰：「吾思可以鎮榆林者，莫過杜彥。

translations.literal: Several days later the emperor said: "Of those I consider able to hold Yulin, none surpasses Du Yan."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he said, "Of all those fit to secure Yulin, none surpasses Du Yan."

sentences.zh: 」於是征拜雲州總管。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned and appointed governor-general of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was then recalled and appointed governor-general of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥來寇，彥輒擒斬之，北夷畏憚，胡馬不敢至塞。

translations.literal: When Turks came to raid, Yan always captured and executed them; the northern tribes feared and respected him, and Turkic horses dared not approach the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Turks raided, Yan captured and executed the raiders. The northern tribes came to fear him, and Turkic horsemen no longer dared approach the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後數年，朝廷複追錄前功，賜子寶虔爵承縣公。

translations.literal: Years later the court again recorded his former merits and granted his son Baoqian the title Duke of Cheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later the court again registered his past service, and his son Baoqian was ennobled as Duke of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遼東之役，以行軍總管從漢王至營州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, as campaign commander he followed the Prince of Han to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, during the Liaodong campaign, he served as campaign commander and followed the Prince of Han as far as Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以彥曉習軍旅，令總統五十營事。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yan was versed in military affairs, ordered him to oversee the affairs of fifty camps.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yan's mastery of military affairs, the emperor put him in overall charge of fifty encampments.

sentences.zh: 及還，拜朔州總管。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed governor-general of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made governor-general of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥複寇雲州，上令楊素擊走之，是後猶恐為邊患，以彥素為突厥所憚，複拜雲州總管。

translations.literal: Turks again raided Yunzhou; the emperor ordered Yang Su to drive them off; thereafter still fearing border trouble, because Yan was habitually feared by the Turks, he was again appointed governor-general of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Yunzhou again, the emperor sent Yang Su to repel them. He still feared further border trouble, and because the Turks had long dreaded Yan, Yan was again appointed governor-general of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾征還，卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: Before long, recalled on account of illness, he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he was recalled because of illness and died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 子寶虔，大業末，文城郡丞。

translations.literal: His son Baoqian, at the end of Daye, was assistant administrator of Wencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoqian, at the close of the Daye era, was assistant administrator of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 高勱高勱，字敬德，渤海蓚人也，齊太尉、清河王嶽之子也。

translations.literal: Gao Mai—Gao Mai, styled Jingde, was a native of Su in Bohai, son of Qi grand commandant and Prince of Qinghe, Gao Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mai, courtesy name Jingde, was from Su in Bohai—the son of Gao Yue, grand commandant of Qi and Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，美風儀，以仁孝聞，為齊顯祖所愛。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, of fine bearing, renowned for benevolence and filial piety, and beloved by Qi Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted and handsome, famed for his filial devotion, and a favorite of Emperor Xianzu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，襲爵清河王。

translations.literal: At age seven he inherited the title Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he succeeded to the title Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 十四為青州刺史，曆右衛將軍、領軍大將軍、祠部尚書、開府儀同三司，改封樂安王。

translations.literal: At fourteen he became inspector of Qingzhou, passed through general of the Right Guards, commander-in-chief of the palace guards, minister of temple affairs, and director of departments of the third rank of yitong, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Lean.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was made inspector of Qingzhou, and went on to hold the posts of general of the Right Guards, commander-in-chief of the palace guards, minister of temple affairs, and director of departments of the third rank of yitong; he was then re-created Prince of Lean.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，有才幹，甚為時人所重。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and firm, possessed talent and ability, and was greatly esteemed by men of his time.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright by nature, capable and forceful, and widely respected.

sentences.zh: 斛律明月雅敬之，每有征伐，則引之為副。

translations.literal: Hulu Guang held him in high esteem; whenever there was a campaign he would take him as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Guang held him in the highest regard and routinely took him as his second-in-command on campaign.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary and right vice-minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and right vice-minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及後主為周師所敗，勱奉太后歸鄴。

translations.literal: When the later sovereign was defeated by Zhou troops, Mai escorted the empress dowager back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: After the later sovereign was routed by Zhou forces, Mai escorted the empress dowager back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 時宦官放縱，儀同苟子溢尤稱寵倖，勱將斬之以徇。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs were unrestrained; the yitong Gou Ziyi was especially said to enjoy favored intimacy; Mai was about to behead him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs ran rampant at court; the yitong Gou Ziyi was said above all to enjoy imperial favor, and Mai was on the point of executing him as an example.

sentences.zh: 太后救之，乃釋。

translations.literal: The empress dowager saved him, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager intervened and Mai spared him.

sentences.zh: 劉文殊竊謂勱曰：「子溢之徒，言成禍福，何得如此！

translations.literal: Liu Wenshu secretly said to Mai: "Ziyi's sort—whose words decide fortune and calamity—how can you go so far!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenshu whispered to him, "Men like Ziyi can make or break fortunes with a word—how can you go so far!"

sentences.zh: 」勱攘袂曰：「今者西寇日侵，朝貴多叛，正由此輩弄權，致使衣冠解體。

translations.literal: Mai rolled up his sleeves and said: "Nowadays western enemies daily encroach, court nobles frequently rebel—precisely because this lot manipulate power, causing the gentry to lose cohesion."
translations.idiomatic: Mai flung up his sleeves and said, "The western enemy presses closer every day and so many of the great families have gone over to the enemy. It is precisely because men like these abuse power that the ruling elite has come apart."

sentences.zh: 若得今日殺之，明日受誅，無所恨也。

translations.literal: If I can kill him today and be executed tomorrow, I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If I can kill him today and die for it tomorrow, I shall have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 」文殊甚愧。

translations.literal: Wenshu was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 既至鄴，勱勸後主：「五品已上家累，悉置三台之上，因脅之曰：'若戰不捷，則燒之。

translations.literal: Having reached Ye, Mai advised the later sovereign: "Families of fifth rank and above—all their dependents—place them entirely atop the Three Terraces, and coerce them saying: 'If battle does not succeed, then burn them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Once they had reached Ye, Mai urged the sovereign, "Place the families of all officials of the fifth rank and above on the Three Terraces and threaten them: if we do not win the battle, we shall burn them."

sentences.zh: '此輩惜妻子，必當死戰，可敗也。

translations.literal: 'This lot cherish wife and children—they will certainly fight to the death; the enemy can be defeated.'
translations.idiomatic: They cherish their wives and children and will fight to the death—we can defeat the enemy that way."

sentences.zh: 」後主不從，遂棄鄴東遁。

translations.literal: The later sovereign did not follow, and abandoned Ye fleeing east.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign refused, abandoned Ye, and fled east.

sentences.zh: 勱恆後殿，為周軍所得。

translations.literal: Mai always brought up the rear and was taken by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mai covered the rear and was captured by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 武帝見之，與語，大悅，因問齊亡所由。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him, conversed with him, was greatly pleased, and therefore asked the cause of Qi's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou received him, spoke with him, and was greatly pleased; he then asked why Qi had fallen.

sentences.zh: 勱發言流涕，悲不自勝，帝亦為之改容。

translations.literal: Mai as he spoke wept streaming tears, grief overcoming himself; the emperor also changed expression on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Mai spoke through tears, overcome with grief, and the emperor's countenance softened in response.

sentences.zh: 授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of departments of the third rank of yitong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of departments of the third rank of yitong.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，謂勱曰：「齊所以亡者，由任邪佞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor, he said to Mai: "The reason Qi perished was employing wicked flatterers."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor, he told Mai, "Qi fell because it entrusted wicked flatterers."

sentences.zh: 公父子忠良，聞於鄰境，宜善自愛。

translations.literal: You father and son are loyal and good, renowned in neighboring territories—you should take good care of yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Your father and you have been known far and wide for loyalty and integrity; look well to yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」勱再拜謝曰：「勱亡齊末屬，世荷恩榮，不能扶危定傾，以致淪覆。

translations.literal: Mai bowed twice in thanks and said: "Mai is a remnant subordinate of fallen Qi; my family received imperial grace and glory generation after generation; I could not support the tottering and settle the overturning, leading to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Mai bowed twice and replied, "I am a survivor of fallen Qi, one whose house has long enjoyed imperial favor; I failed to shore up a tottering state, and thus brought ruin upon it."

sentences.zh: 既蒙獲宥，恩幸已多，況複濫叨名位，致速官謗。

translations.literal: Having received pardon, favor is already ample; how much more to accept name and rank wantonly, hastening official censure."
translations.idiomatic: I have already received far more mercy than I deserve; how much more shameful would it be to accept rank and title I do not merit and invite censure from the officials."

sentences.zh: 」高祖甚器之，以勱檢校揚州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu greatly valued him and put Mai in charge of inspecting Yangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed and put him in charge of Yangzhou as acting administrator.

sentences.zh: 後拜楚州刺史，民安之。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed inspector of Chuzhou and the people were settled under him.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed inspector of Chuzhou, where the people lived in peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 先是，城北有伍子胥廟，其俗敬鬼。

translations.literal: Previously north of the city there was a shrine to Wu Zixu; local custom revered spirits.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city stood a shrine to Wu Zixu, and the local custom was to lavish offerings on spirits.

sentences.zh: 祈禱者必以牛酒，至破產業。

translations.literal: Those who prayed invariably used cattle and wine, to the point of bankrupting their estates.
translations.idiomatic: Worshippers had to bring cattle and wine, often until their households were ruined.

sentences.zh: 勱歎曰：「子胥賢者，豈宜損百姓乎？

translations.literal: Mai sighed and said: "Zixu was a worthy man—how should he harm the common people?"
translations.idiomatic: Mai sighed and said, "Wu Zixu was a worthy man—would he truly want the people harmed in his name?"

sentences.zh: 」乃告諭所部，自此遂止，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he announced and instructed his jurisdiction; from then on it ceased, and the common people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He issued orders throughout his district, and the practice stopped; the people were greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉光州刺史，上取陳五策，又上表曰：「臣聞夷凶翦暴，王者之懋功；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to inspector of Guangzhou; he presented five stratagems against Chen, and further submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that subduing barbarians and cutting down the violent is the meritorious work of a true king;"
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to inspector of Guangzhou. He submitted five plans against Chen and added a memorial: "I have heard that subduing the barbarous and cutting down the violent is the crowning achievement of a true king;"

sentences.zh: 取亂侮亡，往賢之雅誥。

translations.literal: taking advantage of disorder to strike the perishing is the elegant instruction of past sages.
translations.idiomatic: and that seizing upon disorder to strike the doomed is the ancient lesson of the sages."

sentences.zh: 是以苗民逆命，爰興兩階之舞；

translations.literal: Therefore when the Miao people defied orders, thereupon arose the dance of the two staircases;
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao defied the mandate, the dance of the two staircases was performed;

sentences.zh: 有扈不賓，終召六師之伐。

translations.literal: when Youhu failed in submission, ultimately the six armies' expedition was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: when Youhu refused allegiance, the six hosts were finally called out to chastise them.

sentences.zh: 皆所以寧一宇內，匡濟群生者也。

translations.literal: all are means to secure tranquillity within the four seas and to succor and deliver the multitude of living beings.
translations.idiomatic: All to secure peace under heaven and succor the people.

sentences.zh: 自昔晉氏失馭，天網絕維，群凶於焉蝟起，三方因而鼎立。

translations.literal: Since olden times when the Jin house lost the reins, heaven's net snapped its strands, multitudes of villains thereupon rose like hedgehogs, and the three directions thereby stood like a tripod.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Jin house lost the mandate, the bonds of rule were broken, rebels swarmed like hedgehogs, and the realm split into three contending powers.

sentences.zh: 陳氏乘其際運，拔起細微，茜頊縱其長蛇，竊據吳會；

translations.literal: The Chen clan seized that opportune fortune, sprang up from humble origins, Chen Baxian loosened his long serpent, and stealthily held Wu and Hui;
translations.idiomatic: The house of Chen seized its moment, rose from humble origins, and Chen Baxian, like a coiled serpent, seized Wu and the lower Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 叔寶肆其昏虐，毒被金陵。

translations.literal: Shubao indulged his benighted cruelty, poison spreading over Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: while Chen Shubao has grown ever more cruel and debauched, spreading misery through Jinling.

sentences.zh: 數年已來，荒悖滋甚。

translations.literal: In recent years wanton perversity has grown ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years his excesses have only worsened.

sentences.zh: 牝雞司旦，昵近奸回，尚方役徒，積骸千數，疆埸防守，長戍三年。

translations.literal: The hen announces the dawn, he draws near wicked traitors, artisans of the imperial workshops—their piled bones number in thousands, frontier garrison defence—long service three years.
translations.idiomatic: Women rule at dawn; he dotes on wicked minions; corpses of conscripts from the imperial workshops lie in heaps by the thousands; frontier garrisons serve three-year tours without relief.

sentences.zh: 或微行暴露，沉湎王侯之宅；

translations.literal: Sometimes he travels incognito in coarse dress, plunging into the mansions of princes and marquises;
translations.idiomatic: He goes abroad in disguise and debauches himself in the houses of princes;

sentences.zh: 或賓士駿騎，顛墜康衢之首。

translations.literal: sometimes guests on fine steeds and fleet coursers tumble and fall at the head of the broad highway.
translations.idiomatic: or races fine horses and is thrown headlong in the public streets.

sentences.zh: 有功不賞，無辜獲戮，烽燧日警，未以為虞，耽淫靡嫚，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Merit goes unrewarded, the innocent suffer execution, beacon-fires daily alarm yet he takes no thought for worry, addicted to lust and dissipation without knowing bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Merit goes unrewarded and the innocent are killed; beacon-fires rise daily yet he feels no alarm; he wallows in debauchery without limit.

sentences.zh: 天厭亂德，妖實人興，或空裡時有大聲，或行路共傳鬼怪，或刳人肝以祠天狗，或自捨身以厭妖訛。

translations.literal: Heaven detests disorderly virtue, portents verify and men arise—sometimes great sounds in empty air, sometimes travellers jointly spreading tales of demons, sometimes flaying human livers to sacrifice to the celestial dog, sometimes casting away one's body to suppress omens of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has grown weary of his conduct and omens multiply—strange cries in the air, demons reported on the roads, human livers cut out to appease the celestial dog, bodies offered to ward off evil signs.

sentences.zh: 民神怨憤，災異薦發，天時人事，昭然可知。

translations.literal: People and spirits resent and rage, disasters and prodigies repeatedly erupt—heaven's seasons and human affairs are plainly knowable.
translations.idiomatic: The people and the spirits alike resent him; disasters multiply; the signs in heaven and on earth are plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸才，猥蒙朝寄，頻曆籓任，與其鄰接，密邇仇讎，知其動靜，天討有罪，此即其時。

translations.literal: Your servant with mediocre talent, undeservedly entrusted by the court, repeatedly holding frontier posts, adjoining them closely, near at hand to the foe—I know their movements; heaven's punishment of guilt—this is the hour.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of little talent, yet the court has repeatedly entrusted me with border posts adjoining Chen; I know their movements well. Heaven's judgment falls on the guilty—now is the time.

sentences.zh: 若戎車雷動，戈船電邁，臣難驚怯，請效鷹犬。

translations.literal: If war chariots thunder like lightning and armed boats flash forward, your servant, though hard pressed by fear, asks to serve as hawk and hound."
translations.idiomatic: When the war-chariots roll like thunder and the war-fleet strikes like lightning, though I am no bold warrior, I beg to serve as your hound."

sentences.zh: 」高祖覽表嘉之，答以優詔。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, replying with an excellent edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with approval and answered with a commendatory decree.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以勱為行軍總管，從宜陽公王世積下陳江州。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Mai was made campaign commander following the Duke of Yiyang, Wang Shiji, down on Chen's Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the great invasion of Chen was launched, Mai served as campaign commander under Wang Shiji, Duke of Yiyang, descending on Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以功拜上開府，賜物三千段。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed upper director of departments and granted three thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made upper director of departments and given three thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 隴右諸羌數為寇亂，朝廷以勱有威名，拜洮州刺史。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Longyou repeatedly raided in disorder; the court because Mai had a powerful reputation appointed him inspector of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang tribes of Longyou had repeatedly raided, and because Mai's reputation for severity was well known, he was appointed inspector of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 下車大崇威惠，民夷悅附，其山谷間生羌相率詣府稱謁，前後至者，數千餘戶。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he greatly esteemed both authority and kindness; Chinese and tribesmen gladly attached themselves; raw Qiang in mountain valleys in groups came to the prefecture to pay court—in all those who came before and after numbered more than several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he combined stern authority with generous kindness, and both Chinese and tribesmen willingly submitted. Raw Qiang from the valleys came in groups to pay homage at his yamen—several thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 豪猾屏跡，路不拾遺，在職數年，稱為治理。

translations.literal: Powerful scoundrels hid their traces, goods on the road were not picked up; during several years in office he was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Local bullies vanished, lost goods lay untouched on the roads, and for several years his district was celebrated as well governed.

sentences.zh: 後遇吐谷渾來寇，勱遇疾不能拒戰，賊遂大掠而去。

translations.literal: Later when Tuyuhun came raiding, Mai encountered illness and could not resist battle; the bandits thereupon plundered greatly and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tuyuhun invaded, Mai was ill and unable to fight; the enemy raided heavily and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 憲司奏勱亡失戶口，又言受羌饋遺，竟坐免官。

translations.literal: The censorate memorialized that Mai had lost household registers, also saying he received Qiang bribes, and in the end he was dismissed from office on account of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate charged him with losing population records and accepting gifts from the Qiang; he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後卒于家，時年五十六。

translations.literal: Later he died at home, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 子士廉，最知名。

translations.literal: His son Shilian was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilian was the best known.

sentences.zh: 爾朱敞爾硃敞，字乾羅，秀容契胡人，爾硃榮之族子也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Chang—Erzhu Chang, styled Qianluo, a Qihu man of Xiurong, was a clansman's son of Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Chang, courtesy name Qianluo, was a Qihu tribesman from Xiurong and a clansman of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 父彥伯，官至司徒、博陵王。

translations.literal: His father Yanbo reached the post of minister of education and Prince of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanbo rose to minister of education and Prince of Boling.

sentences.zh: 齊神武帝韓陵之捷，盡誅爾硃氏，敞小，隨母養于宮中。

translations.literal: When Qi Emperor Shenwu won at Hanling, the Erzhu clan was entirely executed; Chang was young and followed his mother, raised in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shenwu of Qi's victory at Hanling, the entire Erzhu clan was slaughtered. Chang was still a boy and was raised in the palace with his mother.

sentences.zh: 及年十二，自竇而走，至於大街，見童兒群戲者，敞解所著綺羅金翠之服，易衣而遁。

translations.literal: At age twelve he fled from a hole in the wall, reaching the great street; seeing children playing in groups, Chang removed the fine silk, brocade, gold, and kingfisher garments he wore and exchanged clothes to escape.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he broke out through a hole in the wall and came to the main street. Seeing children at play in a group, he stripped off his silks and jeweled finery and traded clothes with one of them to slip away.

sentences.zh: 追騎尋至，初不識敞，便執綺衣兒。

translations.literal: Pursuing horsemen soon arrived; at first not recognizing Chang, they seized the child in fine clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers soon arrived; they did not recognize Chang at first and seized the child in the fine garments instead.

sentences.zh: 比究問知非，會日已暮，由是得免。

translations.literal: By the time inquiry revealed it was not him, dusk had already fallen, and thereby he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before they realized their mistake, night had fallen, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 遂入一村，見長孫氏媼踞胡床而坐。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered a village and saw an old woman of the Changsun clan seated on a folding stool.
translations.idiomatic: He came to a village and found an old woman of the Changsun clan seated on a folding stool.

sentences.zh: 敞再拜求哀，長孫氏湣之，藏於複壁。

translations.literal: Chang bowed twice begging pity; the Changsun lady pitied him and hid him in a double wall.
translations.idiomatic: Chang bowed to her in appeal for mercy; pitying him, she hid him in a concealed chamber within the wall.

sentences.zh: 三年，購之愈急，跡且至，長孫氏曰：「事急矣，不可久留。

translations.literal: Three years on, the reward for his capture grew ever more urgent and his trail was nearly upon him; the Changsun lady said: "The matter is urgent—you cannot stay long."
translations.idiomatic: After three years the manhunt intensified and pursuers were closing in. The Changsun lady said, "This has become urgent—you cannot remain here."

sentences.zh: 」資而遣之。

translations.literal: She supplied him and sent him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: She gave him provisions and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 遂詐為道士，變姓名，隱嵩山，略涉經史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pretended to be a Daoist priest, changed his name, hid on Mount Song, and dabbled in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He then passed himself off as a Daoist priest, assumed a new name, and lived in seclusion on Mount Song, reading a little in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，人頗異之。

translations.literal: Within several years people found him rather unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the locals came to regard him as something out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 嘗獨坐岩石之下，泫然而歎曰：「吾豈終於此乎？

translations.literal: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he burst into tears and sighed: "How can I end my days here?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed, "Am I to finish my life like this?"

sentences.zh: 伍子胥獨何人也！

translations.literal: What sort of man was Wu Zixu alone!
translations.idiomatic: What was Wu Zixu, that he alone could not do the same!

sentences.zh: 」於是間行微服，西歸於周。

translations.literal: Thereupon he traveled by secret paths in plain dress and returned west to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then made his way west to Zhou by back roads and in disguise.

sentences.zh: 太祖見而禮之，拜大都督、行台郎中，封靈壽縣伯，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu saw and honored him, appointed him grand commander and acting director of the mobile administration, enfeoffed him as Baron of Lingshou with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu received him with honor, appointed him grand commander and acting director of the mobile administration, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Lingshou with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷通直散騎常侍，轉車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regular attendant and supernumerary cavalry constant attendant, then to chariot-and-cavalry grand general and director of departments of the third rank of yitong, and advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regular attendant and supernumerary cavalry constant attendant, then to chariot-and-cavalry grand general and director of departments of the third rank of yitong, and advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 保定中，遷使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was transferred to bearer of credentials, chief general of swift cavalry, and director of departments of the third rank of yitong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoding era he was made bearer of credentials, chief general of swift cavalry, and director of departments of the third rank of yitong.

sentences.zh: 天和中，增邑五百戶，曆信、臨、熊、潼四州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era his fief increased by five hundred households; he served as inspector of Xin, Lin, Xiong, and Tong, and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era his fief was increased by five hundred households; he served as inspector of Xin, Lin, Xiong, and Tong, and was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 武帝東征，上表求從，許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned east, he submitted a memorial requesting to follow; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched east, he submitted a memorial asking to accompany the campaign and was permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 攻城陷陣，所當皆破，進位上開府。

translations.literal: Storming cities and breaking formations, wherever he went he prevailed; he advanced to upper director of departments.
translations.idiomatic: In storming cities and breaking enemy lines he prevailed wherever he fought and was raised to upper director of departments.

sentences.zh: 除南光州刺史，入為護軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed inspector of southern Guangzhou, then entered the capital as protector-general grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed inspector of southern Guangzhou and later entered the capital as protector-general grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉膠州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was transferred to inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 於是迎長孫氏及弟置於家，厚資給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he welcomed the Changsun lady and his younger brother into his home and generously provided for them.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought the Changsun lady and his younger brother into his household and supported them generously.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，改封邊城郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the mandate, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Biancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, his title was changed to Duke of Biancheng.

sentences.zh: 黔安蠻叛，命敞討平之。

translations.literal: The Qian'an tribes rebelled; he was ordered to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Qian'an rebelled, he was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 師旋，拜金州總管。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed governor-general of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed governor-general of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋轉徐州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor-general of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor-general of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，號為明肅，民吏懼之。

translations.literal: During several years in office he was known as clear and stern; people and officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: For several years in office he was known for clarity and severity, and both people and officials stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 後以年老，上表乞骸骨，賜二馬軺車，歸於河內，卒于家，時年七十二。

translations.literal: Later, because of old age, he submitted a memorial begging to retire; he was granted two horse-drawn light carriages, returned to Hedong, and died at home, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Later, citing his age, he asked to retire; the court granted him two light carriages, he returned to Hedong, and died at home at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子最嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zui succeeded to his line.

sentences.zh: 周搖周搖，字世安，其先與後魏同源，初為普乃氏，及居洛陽，改為周氏。

translations.literal: Zhou Yao—Zhou Yao, styled Shi'an; his ancestors were of the same origin as Later Wei; originally of the Punai clan, and upon settling in Luoyang they changed to the Zhou surname.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yao, courtesy name Shi'an, came from the same stock as Later Wei: his clan had originally been the Punai, and after settling in Luoyang they adopted the surname Zhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖拔拔，祖右六肱，俱為北平王。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Baba and grandfather Youliugun were both Princes of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Baba and grandfather Youliugun had both been Princes of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 父恕延，曆行台僕射、南荊州總管。

translations.literal: His father Shuyan had served as vice minister of the mobile administration and governor-general of southern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuyan had served as vice minister of the mobile administration and governor-general of southern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 搖少剛果，有武藝，性謹厚，動遵法度。

translations.literal: Yao in youth was firm and resolute, possessed martial skill, and by nature was discreet and sincere; in conduct he always observed the law.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yao was firm and resolute, skilled in arms, discreet and sincere by nature, and scrupulous in observing the law.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，官至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He served Wei and rose to director of departments of the third rank of yitong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei service he rose to director of departments of the third rank of yitong.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，賜姓車非氏，封金水郡公。

translations.literal: When Zhou Emperor Min received the mandate, he was granted the surname Chefei and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou took the throne, he was granted the surname Chefei and created Duke of Jinshui.

sentences.zh: 曆夙、楚二州刺史，吏民安之。

translations.literal: He served as inspector of Su and Chu, and officials and people lived in peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inspector of Su and Chu, where officials and people alike were content under his rule.

sentences.zh: 從帝平齊，每戰有功，超授柱國，進封夔國公。

translations.literal: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, in every battle he had merit; he was exceptionally appointed pillar of state and advanced to Duke of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: In the pacification of Qi he distinguished himself in every battle, was exceptionally made pillar of state, and was advanced to Duke of Kui.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜晉州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed governor-general of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed governor-general of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時高祖為定州總管，文獻皇后自京師詣高祖，路經搖所，主禮甚薄。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozu was governor-general of Dingzhou; the Empress Dowager Wenxian came from the capital to visit him, passing through Yao's post, where the reception was very sparse.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Gaozu was governor-general of Dingzhou. When Empress Dowager Wenxian traveled from the capital to visit him and passed through Yao's jurisdiction, his hospitality was notably plain.

sentences.zh: 既而白後曰：「公廨甚富於財，限法不敢輒費。

translations.literal: Afterward he told the empress: "The official residence is very rich in funds, but restricted by law I dare not spend freely."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he explained to the empress, "The government offices here are well supplied with funds, but the law forbids me to spend them freely."

sentences.zh: 又王臣無得效私。

translations.literal: "Moreover a king's subject may not offer private favors."
translations.idiomatic: "Besides, a subject of the throne may not offer private favors."

sentences.zh: 」其質直如此。

translations.literal: His plain honesty was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his plain honesty.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其奉法，每嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because he observed the law, always praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu always praised him for his strict adherence to the law.

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，徙封濟北郡公，尋拜豫州總管。

translations.literal: When he became grand chancellor his enfeoffment was moved to Duke of Jibei commandery; soon he was appointed governor-general of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he became grand chancellor his title was changed to Duke of Jibei, and he was soon appointed governor-general of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，複姓周氏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the mandate, he reverted to the Zhou surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, he resumed the surname Zhou.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，突厥寇邊，燕、薊多被其患，前總管李崇為虜所殺，上思所以鎮之，臨朝曰：「無以加周搖者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Turks raided the frontier and Yan and Ji suffered greatly; the previous governor-general Li Chong was killed by the barbarians; the emperor pondered how to secure the post and said at court: "None can be placed above Zhou Yao."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier, and Yan and Ji suffered heavily. The previous governor-general Li Chong had been killed by the enemy. The emperor considered how best to secure the region and said at court, "No one is better suited than Zhou Yao."

sentences.zh: 」拜為幽州總管六州五十鎮諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor-general of Youzhou over six prefectures and fifty garrisons with overall military authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor-general of Youzhou with authority over six prefectures, fifty garrisons, and all related military affairs.

sentences.zh: 搖修鄣塞，謹斥候，邊民以安。

translations.literal: Yao repaired border walls and watchtowers, kept strict scouts, and the frontier people were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yao repaired the border defenses, maintained strict scouting, and the frontier people lived in security.

sentences.zh: 後六載，徙為壽州。

translations.literal: Six years later he was transferred to Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was transferred to Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，自以年老，乞骸骨，上召之。

translations.literal: Earlier, deeming himself old, he had begged to retire; the emperor summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, believing himself too old for office, he had asked to retire, and the emperor summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 既引見，上勞之曰：「公積行累仁，曆仕三代，克終富貴，保茲遐壽，良足善也。

translations.literal: After being received in audience, the emperor comforted him: "You accumulated conduct and piled up benevolence, served through three dynasties, attained final wealth and honor, and preserved this long life—truly admirable."
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, the emperor comforted him: "You have heaped up merit through many years of service, held office under three dynasties, attained wealth and honor to the end, and preserved a long life—this is truly admirable."

sentences.zh: 」賜坐褥，歸於第。

translations.literal: He was granted a seat cushion and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a seat cushion and sent home.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，終於家，諡曰恭，時年八十四。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died at home; his posthumous title was Gong; he was aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died at home. His posthumous title was Gong, and he was eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 獨孤楷獨孤楷，字修則，不知何許人也，本姓李氏。

translations.literal: Du Gukai—Du Gukai, styled Xiuzi; of unknown origin; his original surname was Li.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gukai, courtesy name Xiuzi, was of unknown origin and had originally borne the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 父屯，從齊神武帝與周師戰于沙苑，齊師敗績，因為柱國獨孤信所擒，配為士伍，給使信家，漸得親近，因賜姓獨孤氏。

translations.literal: His father Tun had followed Qi Emperor Shenwu in battle with Zhou troops at Shayuan; the Qi army suffered defeat and he was captured by the pillar of state Du Guxin, assigned as a soldier, given to serve in Xin's household, gradually drew near, and was therefore granted the surname Du Gu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tun had followed Emperor Shenwu of Qi against Zhou forces at Shayuan. After the Qi army was defeated, he was captured by the pillar of state Du Guxin, assigned as a soldier in Xin's household, gradually won his trust, and was granted the surname Du Gu.

sentences.zh: 楷少謹厚，便弄馬槊，為宇文護執刀，累轉車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Kai in youth was discreet and sincere and skilled at wielding the cavalry lance; he served as blade-carrier for Yuwen Hu and was repeatedly promoted to chariot-and-cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Kai was discreet and sincere and skilled with the cavalry lance. He served as blade-carrier for Yuwen Hu and rose repeatedly to chariot-and-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 其後數從征伐，賜爵廣阿縣公，邑千戶，拜右侍下大夫。

translations.literal: Afterward he often followed campaigns; he was granted the title Duke of Guang'a county with a fief of a thousand households and appointed right attendant lower grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He later took part in many campaigns, was created Duke of Guang'a with a fief of a thousand households, and appointed right attendant lower grandee.

sentences.zh: 週末，從韋孝寬平淮南，以功賜子景雲爵西河縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan; for merit his son Jingyun was granted the title Duke of Xihe county.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhou he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan, and for his achievements his son Jingyun was ennobled as Duke of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，進授開府，每督親信兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor he was further appointed director of departments and always supervised the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor he was further made director of departments and regularly commanded the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜右監門將軍，進封汝陽郡公。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the mandate he was appointed right gate-guard general and advanced to Duke of Ruyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the mandate was received he was appointed right gate-guard general and advanced to Duke of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 數歲，遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to right guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to right guard general.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，出為原州總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was sent out as governor-general of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renshou he was sent out as governor-general of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀鎮益州，上征之，猶豫未發。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Shu, Xiu, held Yizhou; the emperor summoned him but hesitated to depart.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Shu, Xiu, held Yizhou. The emperor had summoned him, but Xiu hesitated to leave.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐秀生變，拜楷益州總管，馳傳代之。

translations.literal: The court feared Xiu would stir up trouble; Kai was appointed governor-general of Yizhou and hurried by express post to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared Xiu would rebel, so Kai was appointed governor-general of Yizhou and hurried there by express post to replace him.

sentences.zh: 秀果有異志，楷諷諭久之，乃就路。

translations.literal: Xiu indeed harbored other intentions; Kai admonished and persuaded him for a long time until he set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu did indeed harbor rebellious intentions, but after long admonition from Kai he finally set out on the road.

sentences.zh: 楷察秀有悔色，因勒兵為備。

translations.literal: Kai perceived that Xiu regretted his decision and therefore arrayed troops on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kai saw that Xiu looked regretful and therefore kept his troops on alert.

sentences.zh: 秀至興樂，去益州四十餘裡，將反襲楷，密令左右覘所為，知楷不可犯而止。

translations.literal: Xiu reached Xingle, more than forty li from Yizhou, and was about to turn and surprise Kai; he secretly ordered attendants to watch Kai's conduct; knowing Kai could not be violated, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingle, still more than forty li from Yizhou, Xiu was about to turn back and attack Kai. He secretly ordered his men to watch Kai's movements, but seeing that Kai could not be taken by surprise, he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 楷在益州，甚有惠政，蜀中父老於今稱之。

translations.literal: Kai in Yizhou had an excellent record of benevolent administration; the elders of Shu to this day praise him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yizhou Kai governed with notable kindness, and the elders of Shu still praise him to this day.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，轉并州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Kai was transferred to governor-general of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he was transferred to governor-general of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇疾喪明，上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He fell ill and lost his sight, then submitted a memorial begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and lost his sight, then submitted a memorial asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公先朝舊臣，曆職二代，高風素望，臥以鎮之，無勞躬親簿領也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are an old minister of the former court, served through two generations, lofty in conduct and long established in repute—lie in repose to secure the post; there is no need to attend to the ledgers in person."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are an old minister of the former court who served through two reigns, a man of lofty conduct and long-standing repute. Rest where you are and secure the post; you need not attend to the ledgers yourself."

sentences.zh: 」遣其長子淩雲監省郡事。

translations.literal: He sent his eldest son Lingyun to oversee provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his eldest son Lingyun to oversee the affairs of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 數載，轉長平太守，未視事而卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to administrator of Changping and died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to administrator of Changping but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Gong.

sentences.zh: 子淩雲、平雲，彥雲，皆知名。

translations.literal: His sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun were all renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun all became well known.

sentences.zh: 楷弟盛，見《誠節傳》。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Sheng is treated in the the Biography of Loyal Martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's younger brother Sheng is discussed in the the Biography of Loyal Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 乞伏慧乞伏慧，字令和，馬邑鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Qi Fuhui—Qi Fuhui, styled Linghe, a Xianbei of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fuhui, courtesy name Linghe, was a Xianbei from Mayi.

sentences.zh: 祖周，魏銀青光祿大夫，父纂，金紫光祿大夫，並為第一領民酋長。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhou was a Wei silver-gleam grand master for illuminating virtue; his father Zuan was a golden-purple grand master for illuminating virtue; both were first-rank tribal chiefs leading the people.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhou had been a silver-gleam grand master for illuminating virtue in Wei, and his father Zuan a golden-purple grand master for illuminating virtue; both had been first-rank tribal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 慧少慷慨有大節，便弓馬，好鷹犬。

translations.literal: Hui in youth was generous and possessed great integrity; he was skilled at bow and horse and loved hawks and hounds.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Hui was open-handed and high-minded, skilled at archery and horsemanship, and fond of hawking and hunting.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄帝時，為行台左丞，加蕩寇將軍，累遷右衛將軍、太僕卿，自永甯縣公封宜民郡王。

translations.literal: During Qi Emperor Wenxiang he served as left aide of the mobile administration, was added Pacifying-Rebels general, was repeatedly promoted to right guard general and grand master of stud, and advanced from Duke of Yongning county to Prince of Yimin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenxiang of Qi he served as left aide of the mobile administration, was given the additional title Pacifying-Rebels general, rose to right guard general and grand master of stud, and advanced from Duke of Yongning to Prince of Yimin.

sentences.zh: 其兄貴和又以軍功為王，一門二王，稱為貴顯。

translations.literal: His elder brother Guihe also became a prince through military merit; one family held two princely titles and was called noble and prominent.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Guihe also became a prince through military merit, so that one household held two princely titles and was regarded as eminent.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，授使持節、開府儀同大將軍，拜佽飛右旅下大夫，轉熊渠中大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhou Emperor Wu pacified Qi, he was granted bearer of credentials and director of departments equal to great general; he was appointed flying-right-wing lower grandee and transferred to Bear-Brigade middle grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was granted bearer of credentials and director of departments equal to great general, appointed flying-right-wing lower grandee, and transferred to Bear-Brigade middle grandee.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉惇于武陟，所當皆破，授大將軍，賜物八百段。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi; wherever he engaged he prevailed; he was appointed great general and granted eight hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi, prevailed in every engagement, was made great general, and received eight hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 及平尉迥，進位柱國，賜爵西河郡公，邑三千戶，賚物二千三百段。

translations.literal: Upon pacifying Yuwen Jiong he advanced to pillar of state, was granted the title Duke of Xihe commandery with a fief of three thousand households, and was bestowed twenty-three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Yuwen Jiong he was advanced to pillar of state, created Duke of Xihe with a fief of three thousand households, and given twenty-three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 請以官爵讓兄，朝廷不許，論者義之。

translations.literal: He requested to yield rank and title to his elder brother; the court did not permit it; commentators praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to yield his rank and title to his elder brother, but the court refused; commentators praised his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜曹州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the mandate he was appointed inspector of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was appointed inspector of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 曹土舊俗，民多奸隱，戶口名簿帳，恆不以實。

translations.literal: Caozhou had an old custom by which the people often concealed themselves; household registers and name books were habitually not truthful.
translations.idiomatic: Caozhou had long been a place where people concealed themselves from registration, and household records were habitually false.

sentences.zh: 慧下車按察，得戶數萬。

translations.literal: Upon taking office Hui investigated and obtained tens of thousands of households.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Hui conducted an investigation and registered tens of thousands of additional households.

sentences.zh: 遷涼州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor-general of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，突厥屢為寇抄，慧於是嚴警烽燧，遠為斥候，虜亦素憚其名，竟不入境。

translations.literal: Previously the Turks had repeatedly raided; Hui therefore strictly alarmed the beacon-fires and stationed scouts far out; the barbarians also long dreaded his name and ultimately did not cross the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks had long raided the region, but Hui tightened the beacon system and posted scouts far out. The enemy had long dreaded his name and did not cross the border during his tenure.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉齊州刺史，得隱戶數千。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to inspector of Qizhou and obtained several thousand hidden households.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was transferred to inspector of Qizhou and uncovered several thousand hidden households.

sentences.zh: 遷壽州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to governor-general of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年，左轉杞州刺史，在職數年，遷徐州總管。

translations.literal: That year he was demoted to inspector of Qizhou; after several years in office he was transferred to governor-general of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was demoted to inspector of Qizhou; after several years he was transferred to governor-general of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時年逾七十，上表求致仕，不許。

translations.literal: At the time he was past seventy and submitted a memorial requesting retirement, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was over seventy and asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 俄轉荊州總管，又領潭、桂二州總管三十一州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor-general of Jingzhou and also oversaw the governor-generals of Tan and Gui with authority over thirty-one prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor-general of Jingzhou and also given oversight of Tan and Gui and military authority over thirty-one prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其俗輕剽，慧躬行樸素以矯之，風化大洽。

translations.literal: Their custom was flighty; Hui personally practiced plain simplicity to correct it, and customs were greatly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: The local custom was restless and light-minded; Hui corrected it by living plainly himself, and customs were greatly improved.

sentences.zh: 曾見人以穀捕魚者，出絹買而放之，其仁心如此。

translations.literal: Once he saw someone using grain to catch fish; he produced silk to buy and release them—such was his benevolent heart.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw someone using grain to bait fish; he paid out silk to buy the fish and set them free—such was his humane disposition.

sentences.zh: 百姓美之，號其處曰西河公穀。

translations.literal: The people praised him and called his district the Duke of Xihe's Grain.
translations.idiomatic: The people praised him and called the place the Duke of Xihe's Grain.

sentences.zh: 轉秦州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor-general of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，為天水太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne he was made administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne he was made administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，征吐谷渾，郡濱西境，民苦勞役，又遇帝西巡，坐為道不整，獻食疏薄，帝大怒，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, during the campaign against Tuyuhun, the commandery bordered the western frontier; the people suffered forced labor; he also encountered the emperor's western tour; he was punished because the roads were not repaired and the tribute food was sparse and thin; the emperor was greatly enraged and ordered attendants to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye, during the campaign against Tuyuhun, his commandery lay on the western frontier and the people were worn down by forced labor. When the emperor toured the west, Hui was charged with failing to repair the roads and offering meager provisions. The emperor was furious and ordered his attendants to behead him.

sentences.zh: 見其無發，乃釋，除名為民。

translations.literal: Seeing that he had no hair, the emperor released him and stripped him of rank, making him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he was bald, the emperor spared him but struck his name from the rolls and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 張威張威，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei—Zhang Wei, from unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 父琛，魏弘農太守。

translations.literal: His father Chen had been Wei administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen had served as administrator of Hongnong under Wei.

sentences.zh: 威少倜儻有大志，善騎射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Wei in youth was unconstrained and high-minded, skilled at mounted archery, his physical strength surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Wei was free-spirited and ambitious, skilled at horsemanship and archery, and possessed exceptional strength.

sentences.zh: 在周，數從征伐，位至柱國、京兆尹，封長壽縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: In Zhou he often followed campaigns; he rose to pillar of state and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, was enfeoffed Duke of Changshou county with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he took part in many campaigns, rose to pillar of state and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, and was created Duke of Changshou with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 王謙作亂，高祖以威為行軍總管，從元帥梁睿擊之。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian rebelled, Emperor Gaozu made Wei campaign commander to follow the commander-in-chief Liang Rui in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, Emperor Gaozu appointed Wei campaign commander under the commander-in-chief Liang Rui.

sentences.zh: 軍次通穀，謙守將李三王擁勁兵拒守，睿以威為先鋒。

translations.literal: The army halted at Tonggu; Qian's defending general Li Sanwang held elite troops in defense; Rui made Wei vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Tonggu, Qian's defender Li Sanwang held the pass with strong forces. Rui made Wei his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 三王初閉壘不戰，威令人詈侮以激怒之，三王果出陣。

translations.literal: Sanwang at first closed the fortress and would not fight; Wei had men revile and insult to provoke him; Sanwang indeed came out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwang at first kept his gates shut. Wei had men hurl insults to provoke him, and Sanwang finally came out to fight.

sentences.zh: 威令壯士奮擊，三王軍潰，大兵繼至，於是擒斬四千餘人。

translations.literal: Wei ordered stalwarts to strike fiercely; Sanwang's army collapsed; the main force followed; thereupon they captured and beheaded more than four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent his strongest men in a fierce assault; Sanwang's army broke, the main force came up, and more than four thousand of the enemy were captured or killed.

sentences.zh: 進至開遠，謙將趙儼眾十萬，連營三十裡。

translations.literal: Advancing to Kaiyuan, Qian's general Zhao Yan had a host of a hundred thousand, encamped in succession for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Kaiyuan, they found Qian's general Zhao Yan with a force of a hundred thousand, encamped in a line thirty li long.

sentences.zh: 威鑿山通道，自西嶺攻其背，儼遂敗走。

translations.literal: Wei cut a mountain passage, from the western ridge attacked their rear; Yan thereupon fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei cut a road through the mountains and attacked from the western ridge against their rear; Yan was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 追至成都，與謙大戰，威將中軍。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Chengdu, they fought a great battle with Qian; Wei commanded the center army.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Chengdu, they fought a great battle with Qian, with Wei commanding the center.

sentences.zh: 及謙平，進位上柱國，拜瀘州總管。

translations.literal: When Qian was pacified, he advanced to upper pillar of state and was appointed governor-general of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian was subdued, Wei was advanced to upper pillar of state and appointed governor-general of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，曆幽、洛二州總管，改封晉熙郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the mandate he served as governor-general of You and Luo, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jinxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, he served as governor-general of You and Luo and was re-created Duke of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 尋拜河北道行台僕射，後督晉王軍府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice minister of the Hebei circuit mobile administration; later he oversaw the military staff of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice minister of the Hebei circuit mobile administration and later oversaw the military staff of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 數年，拜青州總管，賜錢八十萬，米五百石，雜彩三百段。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed governor-general of Qingzhou and granted eight hundred thousand cash, five hundred shi of grain, and three hundred bolts of miscellaneous silks.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed governor-general of Qingzhou and given eight hundred thousand cash, five hundred shi of grain, and three hundred bolts of silks.

sentences.zh: 威在青州，頗治產業，遣家奴于民間鬻蘆菔根，其奴緣此侵擾百姓。

translations.literal: Wei in Qingzhou rather built up estates; he sent household slaves among the people to sell radish roots, and the slaves on this account harassed the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingzhou Wei built up his private holdings and sent household slaves into the market to sell radish roots; the slaves used this as a pretext to harass the people.

sentences.zh: 上深加譴責，坐廢於家。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply reproached him and he was dismissed to remain at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sternly rebuked him and he was dismissed to remain at home.

sentences.zh: 後從上祠太山，至洛陽，上謂威曰：「自朕之有天下，每委公以重鎮，可謂推赤心矣。

translations.literal: Later, following the emperor in sacrificing at Mount Tai and reaching Luoyang, the emperor said to Wei: "Since I gained the realm I have repeatedly entrusted you with weighty posts—this may be called offering my true heart."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he accompanied the emperor to sacrifice at Mount Tai and reached Luoyang, the emperor said to him, "Since I gained the realm I have repeatedly entrusted you with weighty posts—that was placing my full trust in you."

sentences.zh: 何乃不修名行，唯利是視？

translations.literal: Why then do you not cultivate your reputation and conduct, but look only to profit?"
translations.idiomatic: Why then have you failed to cultivate your reputation and looked only to profit?"

sentences.zh: 豈直孤負朕心，亦且累卿名德。

translations.literal: You not only betray my heart, but also burden your own name and virtue."
translations.idiomatic: You have not only betrayed my trust but also stained your own good name."

sentences.zh: 」因問威曰：「公所執笏今安在？

translations.literal: He then asked Wei: "Where is the tablet you used to hold?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "Where is the court tablet you once held?"

sentences.zh: 」威頓首曰：「臣負罪虧憲，無顏複執，謹藏於家。

translations.literal: Wei bowed his head and said: "Your servant bears guilt and has fallen short of the law; I have no face to hold it again and have kept it carefully at home."
translations.idiomatic: Wei kowtowed and said, "I have offended and fallen short of the law; I had no face to hold it again and have kept it at home."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「可持來。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Bring it here."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Bring it here."

sentences.zh: 」威明日奉笏以見，上曰：「公雖不遵法度，功效實多，朕不忘之。

translations.literal: The next day Wei presented the tablet in audience; the emperor said: "Though you did not observe the law, your achievements are truly many; I do not forget them."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wei presented the tablet. The emperor said, "Though you did not observe the law, your achievements have been many, and I have not forgotten them."

sentences.zh: 今還公笏。

translations.literal: Now I return your tablet."
translations.idiomatic: I now return your tablet to you."

sentences.zh: 」於是複拜洛州刺史，後封睆城郡公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was again appointed inspector of Luozhou and later enfeoffed Duke of Huancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reappointed inspector of Luozhou and later created Duke of Huancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋轉相州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to inspector of Xiangzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to inspector of Xiangzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有子植，大業中，至武賁郎將。

translations.literal: He had a son Zhi who in the Daye era rose to martial-guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, during the Daye era, rose to martial-guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 和洪和洪，汝南人也。

translations.literal: He Hong—He Hong was a native of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He Hong was from Runan.

sentences.zh: 少有武力，勇烈過人。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial strength; his courage and fierceness surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he possessed great physical strength, and his courage and fierceness surpassed other men.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，數從征伐，以戰功累遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: During Zhou Emperor Wu he often followed campaigns; for battle merit he was repeatedly promoted to chariot-and-cavalry grand general and director of departments of the third rank of yitong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he took part in many campaigns and, for his achievements, rose repeatedly to chariot-and-cavalry grand general and director of departments of the third rank of yitong.

sentences.zh: 時龍州蠻任公忻、李國立等聚眾為亂，刺史獨孤善不能禦。

translations.literal: At the time the Longzhou tribesmen Ren Gongxin, Li Guoli, and others gathered crowds in rebellion; the inspector Du Gushan could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Longzhou tribesmen Ren Gongxin and Li Guoli and others gathered forces in rebellion, and the inspector Du Gushan could not repel them.

sentences.zh: 朝議以洪有武略，代善為刺史。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Hong had military strategy and he replaced Shan as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged that Hong had military ability and replaced Shan as inspector.

sentences.zh: 月餘，擒公忻、國立，皆斬首梟之，餘党悉平。

translations.literal: Within a little over a month he captured Gongxin and Guoli, beheaded them both and displayed their heads, and the remaining factions were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a little over a month he captured Gongxin and Guoli, beheaded them and displayed their heads, and the remaining rebels were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 從帝攻河陰，洪力戰，陷其西門。

translations.literal: Following the emperor in attacking Heyin, Hong fought fiercely and stormed the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Heyin he fought fiercely and broke through the western gate.

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，賞物千段。

translations.literal: The emperor admired him and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his valor and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 複從帝平齊，進位上儀同，賜爵北平侯，邑八百戶，拜左勳曹下大夫。

translations.literal: Again following the emperor in pacifying Qi, he advanced to upper yitong, was granted the title Marquis of Beiping with a fief of eight hundred households, and appointed left meritorious-service lower grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was advanced to upper yitong, created Marquis of Beiping with a fief of eight hundred households, and appointed left meritorious-service lower grandee.

sentences.zh: 柱國王軌之擒吳明徹也，洪有功焉，加位開府，遷折衝中大夫。

translations.literal: When the pillar of state Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche, Hong had merit therein; he was added director of departments and transferred to breaker-of-the-enemy middle grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When the pillar of state Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche, Hong distinguished himself and was made director of departments, then transferred to breaker-of-the-enemy middle grandee.

sentences.zh: 尉迥作亂相州，以洪為行軍總管，從韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, Hong was made campaign commander to follow Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Jiong rebelled at Xiangzhou, Hong was made campaign commander under Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 軍至河陽，迥遣兵圍懷州，洪與總管宇文述等擊走。

translations.literal: The army reached Heyang; Jiong sent troops to besiege Huaizhou; Hong with governor-general Yuwen Shu and others drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Heyang, Jiong sent troops to besiege Huaizhou; Hong, with Yuwen Shu and others, drove them off.

sentences.zh: 又破尉惇于武陟。

translations.literal: Again he defeated Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 及平相州，每戰有功，拜柱國，封廣武郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Upon pacifying Xiangzhou, in every battle he had merit; he was appointed pillar of state, enfeoffed Duke of Guangwu commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangzhou was pacified he distinguished himself in every battle, was made pillar of state, and created Duke of Guangwu with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 前後賜物萬段，奴婢五十口，金銀各百挺，牛馬百匹。

translations.literal: Before and after he was granted ten thousand bolts of goods, fifty household slaves, a hundred ingots each of gold and silver, and a hundred head of cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In all he received ten thousand bolts of goods, fifty household slaves, a hundred ingots each of gold and silver, and a hundred head of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 時東夏初平，物情尚梗，高祖以洪有威名，令領冀州事，甚得人和。

translations.literal: At the time eastern Xia had just been pacified and popular sentiment was still unsettled; Emperor Gaozu because Hong had a powerful reputation ordered him to oversee Jizhou affairs, and he greatly won human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern territories had only recently been pacified and popular sentiment was still unsettled. Because Hong's reputation for severity was well known, Emperor Gaozu put him in charge of Jizhou, where he won broad goodwill.

sentences.zh: 數歲，征入朝，為漕渠總管監，轉拜泗州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was summoned to court, served as overseer of the canal-route governor-general, and was transferred to inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled to court, served as overseer of the canal-route governor-general, and was transferred to inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 屬突厥寇邊，詔洪為北道行軍總管，擊走虜，至磧而還。

translations.literal: When Turks raided the frontier, an edict made Hong northern-route campaign commander; he drove off the barbarians and returned upon reaching the desert.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, he was ordered as northern-route campaign commander, drove off the enemy, and returned after reaching the desert.

sentences.zh: 後遷徐州總管，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to governor-general of Xuzhou and died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to governor-general of Xuzhou and died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳穎侯莫陳穎，字遵道，代人也。

translations.literal: Houmo Chenying—Houmo Chenying, styled Zundao, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Houmo Chenying, courtesy name Zundao, was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 與魏南遷，世為列將。

translations.literal: Moving south with Wei, his family for generations were ranked generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved south with Wei, his family for generations had served as ranked generals.

sentences.zh: 父崇，魏、周之際，曆職顯要，官至大司空。

translations.literal: His father Chong, in the transition between Wei and Zhou, held conspicuous posts and rose to grand minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong, in the transition between Wei and Zhou, had held high office and risen to grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 穎少有器量，風神警發，為時輩所推。

translations.literal: Ying in youth had capacity and measure; his spirit and bearing were alert and quick; he was recommended by men of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ying had breadth of character and a keen, commanding presence, and was esteemed by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，以父軍功賜爵廣平侯，累遷開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei Great Unity, for his father's military merit he was granted the title Marquis of Guangping and repeatedly promoted to director of departments of the third rank of yitong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wei Great Unity era he was ennobled as Marquis of Guangping for his father's military merit and rose repeatedly to director of departments of the third rank of yitong.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，從滕王逌擊龍泉、文城叛胡，與柱國豆盧勣各帥兵分路而進。

translations.literal: During Zhou Emperor Wu he followed Prince Teng You in attacking the rebellious Hu of Longquan and Wencheng; with the pillar of state Dou Lu Ji each led troops by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he followed Prince Teng You against the rebellious Hu of Longquan and Wencheng, advancing by separate routes with the pillar of state Dou Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 穎懸軍五百餘裡，破其三柵。

translations.literal: Ying with his army suspended five hundred-odd li and broke their three stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Ying pressed forward more than five hundred li and broke three of their stockades.

sentences.zh: 先是，稽胡叛亂，輒略邊人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Previously, when the Ji Hu rebelled they would seize frontier people as slaves.
