translations.idiomatic: Previously, whenever the Ji Hu rebelled they would seize frontier people as slaves.

sentences.zh: 至是詔胡敢有壓匿良人者誅，籍沒其妻子。

translations.literal: At this time an edict declared that any Hu who dared conceal good commoners would be executed and his wife and children registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict now declared that any Hu who concealed commoners would be executed and his wife and children confiscated.

sentences.zh: 有人言為胡村所隱匿者，勣將誅之，穎謂勣曰：「將在外，君命有所不行。

translations.literal: Someone said they were hidden in a Hu village; Ji was about to execute them; Ying said to Ji: "A general in the field—the ruler's command may in part not be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that people were hidden in a Hu village, Ji was about to execute the villagers. Ying told him, "A general in the field may disregard the ruler's command when necessary."

sentences.zh: 諸胡固非悉反，但相迫脅為亂耳。

translations.literal: The various Hu are certainly not all in rebellion; they were only compelled and coerced into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu are not all rebels; most were forced into rebellion under duress.

sentences.zh: 大兵臨之，首亂者知懼，脅從者思降。

translations.literal: When great armies press upon them, the first to rebel will know fear and those coerced will think of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When a great army presses upon them, the ringleaders will fear and those coerced will wish to surrender.

sentences.zh: 今漸加撫慰，自可不戰而定。

translations.literal: Now if we gradually add soothing comfort, naturally we can secure them without battle.
translations.idiomatic: If we gradually reassure them, we can secure the region without fighting.

sentences.zh: 如即誅之，轉相驚恐，為難不細。

translations.literal: If we immediately execute them, they will in turn alarm one another, and the trouble will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: If we execute them at once, they will panic one another and the trouble will be far greater.

sentences.zh: 未若召其渠帥，以隱匿者付之，令自歸首，則群胡可安。

translations.literal: Better to summon their chieftains, hand over those concealed to them, and order them to surrender of themselves—then the mass of Hu can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to summon their chieftains, hand over those who were hidden to them, and let them surrender on their own; then the Hu can be pacified."

sentences.zh: 」勣從之。

translations.literal: Ji followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Ji followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 群胡感悅，爭來降附，北土以安。

translations.literal: The mass of Hu were moved and pleased, vying to come and submit; the northern lands were thereby secure.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu were moved and pleased, came forward in numbers to submit, and the north was secured.

sentences.zh: 遷司武，加振威中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of martial affairs and added queller-of-awe middle grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of martial affairs and given the additional title queller-of-awe middle grandee.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，拜昌州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor he was appointed inspector of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was grand chancellor he was appointed inspector of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 會受禪，竟不行，加上開府，進爵升平郡公。

translations.literal: Just as the mandate was received he ultimately did not go; he was added upper director of departments and advanced to Duke of Shengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to take up the post the mandate was received; he did not go after all, was made upper director of departments, and advanced to Duke of Shengping.

sentences.zh: 俄拜延州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 數年，轉陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to inspector of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to inspector of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管從秦王俊出魯山道。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, as campaign commander he followed Qin Prince Jun by the Lushan route.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he served as campaign commander under Qin Prince Jun on the Lushan route.

sentences.zh: 屬陳將荀法尚、陳紀降，穎與行軍總管段文振度江安集初附。

translations.literal: When Chen generals Xun Fashang and Chen Ji surrendered, Ying with campaign commander Duan Wenzhen crossed the river to settle the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen generals Xun Fashang and Chen Ji surrendered, Ying and campaign commander Duan Wenzhen crossed the river to settle the newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 尋拜饒州刺史，未之官，遷瀛州刺史，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed inspector of Raozhou; he did not take office and was transferred to inspector of Yingzhou, where he had excellent benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed inspector of Raozhou but did not take up the post; he was transferred to inspector of Yingzhou, where he governed with notable kindness.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，坐與秦王俊交通免官。

translations.literal: During several years in office he was dismissed from office for communicating with Qin Prince Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he was dismissed for communicating with Qin Prince Jun.

sentences.zh: 百姓將送者，莫不流涕，因相與立碑，頌穎清德。

translations.literal: Among the people who came to see him off none did not weep; they therefore jointly erected a stele praising Ying's pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people who came to see him off wept; they jointly erected a stele praising his pure conduct.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校汾州事，俄拜邢州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting administrator of Fenzhou affairs; soon he was appointed inspector of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of Fenzhou as acting administrator; he was soon appointed inspector of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，吏部尚書牛弘持節巡撫山東，以穎為第一。

translations.literal: In Renshou, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, bearing credentials, toured and pacified Shandong and ranked Ying first.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong toured Shandong with imperial credentials and ranked Ying first.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉歎，優詔褒揚。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu admired and sighed and answered with an excellent edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu expressed admiration and issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以嶺南刺史、縣令多貪鄙，蠻夷怨叛，妙簡清吏以鎮撫之，於是征穎入朝。

translations.literal: At the time the court held that the inspectors and county magistrates of Lingnan were mostly greedy and base, and the tribes resented and rebelled; they carefully selected upright officials to pacify them, and therefore summoned Ying to court.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed that the inspectors and magistrates of Lingnan were mostly greedy and that the tribes resented and rebelled; upright officials were sought to pacify the region, and Ying was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 及進見，上與穎言及平生，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Upon being received in audience, the emperor spoke with Ying of their lives together and took it as mirth.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, the emperor spoke with him of their shared past with evident pleasure.

sentences.zh: 數日，進位大將軍，拜桂州總管十七州諸軍事，賜物而遣之。

translations.literal: Several days later he advanced to great general, was appointed governor-general of Guizhou over seventeen prefectures with military authority, was granted goods and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was advanced to great general, appointed governor-general of Guizhou with authority over seventeen prefectures, given gifts, and sent to his post.

sentences.zh: 及到官，大崇恩信，民夷悅服，溪洞生越，多來歸附。

translations.literal: Upon reaching office he greatly esteemed grace and trust; Chinese and tribes were pleased and submitted; Yue of the stream caves in great numbers came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he greatly emphasized grace and trustworthiness; both Chinese and tribes were pleased to submit, and many Yue of the stream valleys came to attach themselves.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，穎兄梁國公芮坐事徙邊，朝廷恐穎不自安，征歸京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Ying's elder brother the Duke of Liang Rui was punished and exiled to the frontier; the court feared Ying would not feel secure and summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Ying's elder brother the Duke of Liang Rui was punished and exiled. The court feared Ying would feel insecure and recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 數年，拜恆山太守。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 其年，嶺南、閩越多不附，帝以穎前在桂州有惠政，為南土所信伏，複拜南海太守。

translations.literal: That year Lingnan and Min-Yue mostly would not submit; the emperor because Ying earlier in Guizhou had benevolent administration and was trusted and submitted to by the southern lands, again appointed him administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: That year much of Lingnan and Min-Yue would not submit. Because Ying's earlier benevolent rule in Guizhou had won the trust of the south, he was again appointed administrator of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 後四歲，卒官。

translations.literal: Four years later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Ding.

sentences.zh: 子虔會，最知名。

translations.literal: His son Qianhui was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianhui was the best known.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：杜彥東夏、南服，屢有戰功，作鎮朔垂，胡塵不起。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Du Yan in eastern Xia and southern domains repeatedly had battle merit; holding the northern frontier, Turkic dust did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Du Yan won repeated victories in the east and south; as warden of the northern frontier he kept the Turkic threat at bay.

sentences.zh: 高勱死亡之際，志氣懍然，疾彼奸邪，致茲餘慶。

translations.literal: Gao Mai at the moment of death, his spirit and resolve were stern; he hated those wicked and treacherous and thereby brought this remaining blessing.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of his fall, Gao Mai's spirit remained unbroken; his hatred of treachery brought lasting honor to his house.

sentences.zh: 爾硃敞幼有權奇，終能止足，崇基墜而複構，不亦仁且智乎！

translations.literal: Erzhu Chang in youth had resourceful strangeness; in the end he could stop in sufficiency; the lofty foundation fell yet was rebuilt—is this not benevolence and wisdom together!
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Chang showed remarkable resourcefulness in youth and in the end knew when to stop; though his house fell, he rebuilt it—was this not both humane and wise?

sentences.zh: 周搖以質實見知，獨孤以恤人流譽，乞伏慧能以國讓，侯莫陳所居治理，或知牧人之道，或踐仁義之路，皆有可稱焉。

translations.literal: Zhou Yao was known for plain substance, Du Gu for compassion winning reputation, Qi Fuhui able to yield the state to his brother, Houmo Chen's posts well governed—some knew the way of shepherding people, some walked the path of benevolence and righteousness; all had what may be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yao was known for plain honesty, Du Gukai for compassion, Qi Fuhui for yielding rank to his brother, and Houmo Chenying for good governance—some knew how to shepherd the people, some walked the path of benevolence and righteousness; each had qualities worth praise.

sentences.zh: 慧以供帳不厚，至於放黜，並結髮登朝，出入三代，終享祿位，不夭性齡，蓋其任心而行，不為矯飾之所致也。

translations.literal: Hui because provisions were not ample came to dismissal; all had bound up their hair and entered court, passed through three dynasties, ultimately enjoyed salary and rank, did not shorten their natural span—probably because they followed their hearts in action and were not caused by affected ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was dismissed because his provisions were deemed insufficient; yet all had entered service young, passed through three dynasties, and enjoyed rank to the end of their natural lives—likely because they acted from the heart rather than from artifice.
